correctness.rationale: The proof classifies all vertices for every parameter chamber, lists every active facet normal, and exhibits one of four fixed directions with strictly negative dot product against the full active normal set. The universal lower bound four follows from separating the origin from the convex hull of fewer illuminating directions. Endpoint normal-cone inequalities prove six and eight are necessary and explicit direction sets attain them. The packaged checker exhausts all chamber sign patterns and endpoint constructions.

originality.rationale: The most relevant 2024 source proves the illumination conjecture for 1-symmetric bodies and a dimension-three bound of six for the applicable non-cubic normalized case, but not this exact four-direction family profile. Close-to-cube literature gives seven, not four. Older Archimedean work uses a different weighted invariant. Focused searches located one exact truncated-octahedron value but no theorem covering the continuous family, cuboctahedron, and truncated cube together.
residual_risks: The solids are classical and the four-direction proof is short, so an equivalent observation could exist under older or unindexed terminology.

One indexed result already covers the regular truncated-octahedron special case at \(c=3/2\); originality is claimed for the full phase profile and the additional special cases, not that isolated value.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete exact phase profile for a natural norm-intersection interpolation between the octahedron and cube, simultaneously determining three classical Archimedean special cases. It reveals a sharp structural phenomenon: one fixed tetrahedral direction set attains the universal dimension-minimum four for every strict mixture, while both endpoint solids have larger illumination numbers.
